title: Doppler Effect
seo_title: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Doppler Effect Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: The Doppler effect with sound: the change in observed frequency when a source moves towards or away from a stationary listener, or a listener moves relative to a stationary source; fL = (v ± vL)/(v ± vs) fs; applications such as ultrasound and speed traps; the red shift of light from galaxies. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Physics: Doppler effect)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the change in pitch of moving sources, the Doppler equation, ultrasound and red shift. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Towards: higher frequency. Away: lower frequency.
key_sub: The frequency of the source itself does not change.
body_html:
How to think about it

When a source of sound moves towards a listener, the wavefronts in front of it are squashed together: the wavelength is shorter and the listener hears a higher frequency. When it moves away, the wavefronts are spread out and the frequency heard is lower. The frequency emitted by the source does not change.

Use fL = (v ± vL)/(v ± vs) × fs, where v is the speed of sound: choose the signs so that the frequency rises when the source and listener get closer. The Doppler effect is used to measure blood flow and the heartbeat of a foetus. Light from distant galaxies is red-shifted, showing that the universe is expanding.

Example

A 500 Hz source approaches at 40 m·s⁻¹ (v = 340 m·s⁻¹). fL?

340/(340 − 40) × 500

Answer: 567 Hz

Example

Light from a galaxy is red-shifted. Is it moving towards us?

Longer wavelengths

Answer: no, it is moving away

Common mistakes

  • Using + for an approaching source in the denominator.
  • Thinking the source's own frequency changes.
  • Mixing up loudness and pitch.

faq.q: Why does the siren's pitch drop suddenly as an ambulance passes?
faq.a: Before it passes it is approaching (higher frequency); after it passes it is moving away (lower frequency).

faq.q: How is the Doppler effect used in medicine?
faq.a: Ultrasound reflected from moving blood cells changes frequency, which shows the speed and direction of blood flow.

items.e: Moving towards the source, the listener meets wavefronts more often, so the frequency rises.

items.q: Does the frequency emitted by the source change when it moves?
c: no, only the frequency the listener detects changes
items.e: The source still vibrates at the same rate; the listener detects a different frequency.

items.q: Which sign is used for v<sub>s</sub> in f<sub>L</sub> = v/(v ± v<sub>s</sub>) f<sub>s</sub> when the source moves towards the listener?
c: no sign; v<sub>s</sub> is left out
items.e: A smaller denominator gives a larger frequency, which is what happens as the source approaches.

to take X-ray photographs of bones
items.e: Ultrasound reflected from moving blood cells changes frequency; the change gives the speed.

items.q: How does a traffic officer's speed trap use the Doppler effect?
c: it times the car between two lines painted on the road
it measures how loud the car is
it photographs the number plate only
it measures the change in frequency of waves reflected from a moving car
items.e: The frequency shift of the reflected radar or laser waves gives the car's speed.

items.q: What is a red shift?
c: light bends towards red near the Sun
light from a galaxy moving away is shifted to longer wavelengths
light from a hot star is red
red light travels faster than blue light
items.e: The Doppler effect for light: a receding source shows longer, redder wavelengths.

items.q: In front of a moving sound source, the wavelength is …
c: longer than when the source is at rest

items.e: The source moves after each wavefront, so wavefronts in front are closer together.

c: yes, it increases by the source's speed
no, it depends only on the medium
items.e: The speed of sound depends on the medium; only the frequency and wavelength observed change.

items.e: Wavefronts are squashed together in front of the moving source, so the frequency is higher.

items.q: In the Doppler formula, what does v stand for?
c: the speed of sound in the medium
items.e: v is the speed of the wave in air, often 340 m·s⁻¹.

items.q: Why does the pitch of a passing car change suddenly, not slowly, at the moment it passes?
c: the sound reflects off the road
the car changes from approaching to moving away
items.e: Before it passes the frequency is higher, after it passes it is lower.

items.q: A source of sound moves towards you. Does the loudness explain the change in pitch?
c: yes; louder sounds have a higher pitch
no; pitch depends on frequency, which changes because of the motion
no; pitch depends on the speed of sound
yes; pitch and loudness are the same
items.e: Loudness depends on amplitude; pitch depends on frequency.

items.q: Which has the longer wavelength: microwaves or radio waves?
items.e: Wavelength decreases from radio waves to gamma rays.

items.q: In the electromagnetic spectrum, which comes between infrared and ultraviolet?

items.q: Which has the longer wavelength: ultraviolet or gamma rays?

items.q: Which electromagnetic waves are used for fibre optic communications?
items.e: Each part of the spectrum has uses that match its properties.
